root_cause.text: In io_wq_remove_pending(), when updating hash_tail[] after cancelling a hashed work, the code does not check whether the predecessor work is also hashed, allowing a non-hashed work (with hash value 0) to be stored in hash_tail[0] and later become a dangling pointer when the non-hashed work is freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an `io_wq_is_hashed(prev_work)` check. The CVE description explains that `io_get_work_hash()` returns 0 for non-hashed work (since hash bits are never set), so a hashed bucket-0 work cancelled with a non-hashed predecessor will spuriously pass the hash comparison, storing the non-hashed work's pointer in `wq->hash_tail[0]`, which later becomes a dangling pointer after the non-hashed work is freed and reused, leading to use-after-free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential incorrect hash tail update by ensuring the previous work is hashed before using its hash value.
intent_record.what: Added a condition to check if prev_work is hashed (io_wq_is_hashed(prev_work)) before comparing its hash value in the hash tail update logic.
intent_record.how: When removing a pending work that is the tail of a hash bucket, the code now only updates the hash tail to prev_work if prev_work is also hashed; otherwise, it sets the tail to NULL, preventing assignment of a non-hashed work as the tail.

candidates.rationale: Assigns a work to hash_tail without verifying that the work is hashed. A non-hashed work (with hash value 0) can be stored here, leading to a dangling pointer when that work is freed.

The condition checks only the hash value equality but does not check if prev_work is hashed. This allows a non-hashed work (with hash 0) to pass the check if the original work's hash is also 0, enabling the vulnerable assignment.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment stores a work in hash_tail[hash] without verifying that the work is hashed. If prev_work is a non-hashed work (hash value 0), it gets placed in hash_tail[0], creating a dangling pointer when that work is later freed, as the hash chain expects only hashed works.

This condition checks only equality of the hash value but does not ensure that prev_work is actually hashed (i.e., part of a hash chain). A non-hashed work may have hash 0, so if the cancelled work's hash is also 0, the condition passes, allowing the vulnerable assignment to a non-hashed work.
